items.title: Discovering the Trans Canada Trail in Mississauga
items.summary: Presented in partnership with the Trans Canada Trail. I’ve lived in Mississauga since August of 1994 and have experienced nearly every part of the city from Meadowvale to Port Credit. ) This year, I decided to dedicate a day to exploring Mississauga’s contribution to the trail through four different locations, all conveniently located on the shores of Lake Ontario. For all the travel that I’ve done in my 15+ year career, I was excited to adventure in my back yard. For reference, the TCT is nearly 30,000 kilometres long and this is my second official experience this year, with the first being in Quebec’s P’tit Train du Nord. THE 2027 SUBARU TRAILSEEKER ELECTRIC VEHICLE AT LAKEFRONT PROMENADE PARK. As I’ve also reviewed new cars for the past 15 years via Modern Motoring, I decided to use an electric vehicle, the 2027 Subaru Trailseeker, as my car for this adventure. In this article, I’ll walk you through the four parts of the trail I did, all of which are accessible and approachable for all ages and capabilities. Whether it’s a short or long voyage by foot or by two wheels, the TCT is a wonderful, free resource that’s available to everyone. On the east side of Mississauga in Lakeview is Lakefront Promenade Park, featuring boat launches, a beach and excellent views of Lake Ontario. It’s also part of Mississauga’s extensive Waterfront Trail. There’s plenty of free parking and you’ll see walkers, joggers, runners and cyclists enjoy this part of the TCT. There’s a boardwalk and wildlife to enjoy, while the balance of the trail is paved for heightened accessibility. Bring your own food and or drink to enjoy along the trail and you can launch your kayak, canoe or standup paddle board.

items.title: 30 new stores and restaurants open at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga
items.summary: Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga is opening more than 30 new retail, dining and lounge locations inside its terminals in what it describes as a “landmark commercial expansion” designed to transform the experience for travellers. The new businesses and restaurants, which combine to create what airport officials say is “a strong lineup of Canadian-owned, Toronto-founded and locally inspired brands alongside internationally recognized names,” are opening throughout 2026. “For millions of travellers each year, Toronto Pearson is where journeys begin, connections are made and Canada comes to life,” Toronto Pearson CEO Deborah Flint said in a news release on Wednesday. ” Toronto Pearson Airport is Canada’s biggest and busiest air hub. Pearson officials said the significant commercial expansion comes as Canada’s biggest and busiest airport “embarks on ambitious plans to modernize and prepare for future growth” through one of the largest airport infrastructure projects in Canadian history. A creation of the Greater Toronto Airports Authority, which runs Pearson, the airport’s multibillion-dollar Long-term Investment in Facilities and Terminals plan (Pearson LIFT) has been in the works for years and promises to modernize and expand Toronto Pearson over the next decade. 5-billion undertaking to modernize Pearson’s two passenger terminals. The contracts for that major project were awarded in July.

items.title: Dog poop problem persists in Mississauga: city
items.summary: Despite repeated attempts the past several years to get more Mississauga dog owners to clean up after their pets in public places, city officials say the messy habit of not doing so continues to cause problems. Citing a difficulty in enforcing the bylaw that deals with dog poop not being properly disposed of (fines of $115 to $180 can be issued), City of Mississauga officials have said their focus instead the past few years has been on hammering home the “stoop and scoop” message via public education efforts. Still, not enough dog owners are heeding the messages and, as a result, numerous unsightly messes can be found in parks and other places across the city. “Dog waste is still causing quite a stink in Mississauga,” the city said on Wednesday in yet another online plea with offenders to change their ways. ” If a waste bin is full, the city continued, “use another or take (the filled poop bag) home and report overflowing bins to 311. Dog waste belongs in garbage bins or designated dog waste stations, which help manage waste more safely and reduce environmental impact. ” Numerous dog waste disposal stations are located across the city. 3 million pounds) of annual waste.

items.title: Brampton home searched after retail theft investigation begins in Mississauga
items.summary: Four Brampton residents are facing numerous charges following an investigation into a series of organized retail thefts across the Greater Toronto Area. The investigation began in Mississauga after Peel Regional Police responded to a reported theft at a business near Clayhill Road and Dundas Street West on June 18. Investigators with the 11 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau identified several suspects and linked them to additional retail thefts throughout Peel Region. On July 20, police executed a search warrant at a residence near Mississauga Road and Mayfield Road in Brampton. Officers say they recovered approximately $15,000 worth of property stolen from several retailers, including fitness, department and pharmacy stores. The recovered items included electronics, health and fitness products, household goods, health supplements and cosmetics. Police also seized two vehicles, jewelry and cash in various currencies. Four Brampton residents were arrested and charged in connection with the investigation. Czuljana Ciecierska, 43, is facing seven counts of theft under $5,000, one count of theft over $5,000, possession of property obtained by crime over $5,000 and laundering proceeds of crime.

items.title: Mississauga warns new Ontario data centre rules still leave cities exposed
items.summary: Ontario’s Data Centre Playbook calls on developers to fund parks and community centres — but Mississauga staff say cities have no legal tools to enforce those commitments. Mississauga city council will vote on an Interim Control Bylaw on Sept. 16 which, if approved, will put a pause on data centres in the city for a year. Mississauga city planning staff are warning that Ontario’s new framework to regulate data centres leaves cities without the legal tools to protect communities from their impacts. A staff report heading to general committee today recommends council formally respond to Ontario’s draft Data Centre Playbook before the public comment period closes Sept. 12. The report comes six weeks after council unanimously voted on July 29 to direct staff to prepare a bylaw that would pause new major data centre applications for one year — a move that would make Mississauga the first GTA municipality to do so, if approved at a final vote Sept. 16. The decision followed community opposition to a proposed Prologis data centre in Meadowvale Business Park, with more than 20 residents raising concerns at the July 29 council meeting about noise, energy demand and proximity to homes. The provincial framework, released Aug. 13, outlines how data centre proposals seeking to connect to the Ontario electricity grid will be evaluated. While city staff say they broadly support provincial efforts to regulate the sector, the report identifies a fundamental disconnect in how the Playbook is written.

items.title: High-tech approach to parking enforcement comes to Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga will soon start using Licence Plate Recognition technology to dish out parking tickets. Starting in October, City of Mississauga parking enforcement will employ the technology to automatically photograph licence plate information from illegally parked vehicles. Tickets will then be mailed to offenders/registered vehicle owners. “This new process supports parking enforcement officers in places where issuing a physical penalty notice on a vehicle may not be effective, such as school zones and time-limited parking zones,” the city said. ” The use of Licence Plate Recognition technology, which the city says will improve safety for parking enforcement officers and enhance how the municipality delivers services, is one of a series of changes to be introduced in October by the city’s parking enforcement division. Also among the new rules is an extended period of time for those who are ticketed to either pay the fine or request a review of the incident and challenge the penalty. Those who receive tickets will now have 30 days, double the current 15-day period, to pay the fine or request a review of the matter. The changes, approved in July by Mississauga city council, are part of an effort to modernize parking enforcement, improve compliance with parking regulations and enhance service delivery efficiency, the City of Mississauga said. The revamped system also includes the mailing out of parking tickets to offenders in addition to the extended timelines to either pay a parking ticket or fight it.

items.title: Every One of Mississauga's Cheapest August Home Sales Was a Condo, Zoocasa Finds
items.summary: According to INsauga, the least expensive home sold in Mississauga last month went for $309,000, according to a Zoocasa analysis of Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data. The outlet reports every one of the least expensive homes sold in August was a condo apartment. INsauga reports the average price for a condo apartment in Mississauga fell to $495,052 in August, down from $511,649 in July and from $549,936 in August 2025. According to the outlet, one of the least expensive sales was a three-bedroom, two-storey condo in Sheridan near the QEW and Clarkson GO Station, which sold for $400,000, above its $384,900 list price. INsauga reports another was an updated one-bedroom condo in City Centre featuring floor-to-ceiling windows, stainless steel appliances and a parking space with a locker.

items.title: Mulaney Says Festival's Postponement Wasn't His Call, Plans Return to the Region Soon
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, comedian John Mulaney says he intends to perform in the Mississauga region soon after the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival he was set to headline was postponed at the last minute. The outlet reports the festival, scheduled to run at Erindale Park from Friday to Sunday, was called off in an Instagram post from organizers on Tuesday. According to the Star, organizers wrote that postponing the show was the right decision to ensure they could deliver the best possible festival, even though they knew there was a lot of excitement around it. The outlet reports Mulaney posted on social media Tuesday night saying the decision to move the festival's dates was not his. According to the Star, organizers are exploring new dates and plan to follow up directly with ticket holders.
